configs.description: EX4600-40F-DC-AFI: two 650 W DC supplies (JPSU-650W-DC-AFI) and five back-to-front fan modules (QFX5100-FAN-AFI).

gaps.wanted: The part number of the four-post rack mount kit and the ear positions. The guide names front mounting rails, rear mounting blades and extension brackets (Table 32) and the datasheet lists a four-post kit with every model, and neither prints a part number.
The Junos names of the SFP+ and QSFP+ ports and of the module ports. The guide held names only em0 and em1 and refers the reader to the Hardware Compatibility Tool for transceivers.

gaps.note: The datasheet (Sep 2021) says "-36 to -72 V DC power"; the guide (2025-08-12), Table 19, says the operating range is -40 VDC through -72 VDC. The guide is the newer and is carried.
gaps.wanted: which lower bound the hardware is rated to, from Juniper

The handle colour and airflow label of the DC supplies. The guide's Table 14 covers the AC pair; the DC supplies take the same orange and blue by relation, not by reading, and no photograph of one is held.

A photograph of a front-to-back build. The rear photograph is a back-to-front build; the AIR OUT fan modules and the AFO supply are drawn from it with the legend and colour of Tables 11 and 14. The photographed AFI supply has a dark handle, not the blue the table gives.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port for image updates. It is drawn with the neutral usb2 skin, because the photograph shows a dark tongue with four contacts.
What the two small lamps above the C1 SFP cage show. Figure 13 and the photograph draw them, and the guide's text and tables do not describe them.

The laser warning label and its hazard mark at the front, the serial number label and the vertical rating legend at the right of the rear are applied or printed small. The rating legend is drawn as read, and the two front labels are reserved as regions.
The depth of the fan modules, the supplies and the expansion modules. The guide's figures are isometric with no scale and its tables give weights of the chassis only.

chassis.note: Guide Table 4: 1.72 in (4.3 cm) high, 17.36 in (44.1 cm) wide, 20.48 in deep, 21.7 lb (9.84 kg) with the power supplies and fan modules installed. The table prints the depth as "20.48 in. (4.37 cm)", a slip; the datasheet gives 1.72 x 17.36 x 20.48 in (4.37 x 44.09 x 52.02 cm), so the height is 43.7 mm, the width 440.9 and the depth 520.2. The width is the body: the brackets extend it to 19 in (Table 23), so they are not modelled.

colour.note: The front plate samples #6a6d71 to #76797d (median of bare patches) and the rear panel #7a7f85. The chassis colour is a mid grey between them. The photographs are lit and these are their values, not a paint reference.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide describes flush and 2 in recessed mounting in a four-post rack with front mounting rails, rear mounting blades and extension brackets (Table 32), and the datasheet lists a four-post rack mount kit with each model. Neither prints a part number for the kit, the library holds no contract for it and none is written, so chassis.ears and chassis.kits are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 440.9 mm chassis without brackets.

esd.note: Guide Figure 9 callout 1, the electrostatic discharge terminal, is the round jack at the lower left, centred 7.2 mm across and 38.4 mm down, with the ESD mark above it at 31.0 mm.

fans-and-supplies.note: The five fan modules (QFX5100-FAN-AFO and QFX5100-FAN-AFI, Table 11) and the two supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AFO and -AFI, Table 14; JPSU-650W-DC-AFO and -AFI, datasheet ordering table) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. The cover panel for an empty supply slot is a component too. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay; the fan in each supply is inside the supply.

gate-1.note: The front photograph's body, between its edges, is 1483 x 148 px, an aspect of 10.02 against the table's 440.9 / 43.7 = 10.09 (0.7 percent out); the rear photograph's is 1454 x 145 px, 10.03 (0.6 percent out). So both are read as orthographic, the front at 3.363 px/mm across and 3.393 down, the rear at 3.298 across and 3.318 down. A pixel is 0.3 mm, so every position read off them is estimated to about 0.5 mm. Guide Figures 9 and 12 are line drawings at 1.66 px/mm and are used to count and to read the printing.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life notice. Two third-party trackers (endoflife.ai, eol.network) report a Juniper notice of 2026-06-29 (TSB109286) with a last order date of 2026-12-29 and end of support on 2031-12-29. The Juniper bulletin itself was not reached, so the dates are estimated.

mgmt-labels.note: The photograph prints CON above the upper RJ-45 jack and C0 below the lower one, with the legend C1 above the SFP cage; guide Figure 13 calls the upper jack the console (CON) and the lower one em0 (C0), and the SFP cage em1 (C1). The photograph and the figure agree.

modules.note: The two bays at the right of the port panel (guide Figure 9 callout 4, "Expansion module bays with cover panels (2)"). The first bay starts at 890 px, 262.4 mm, the seam is at 349.1 mm and the second ends at 435.8 mm; each module face is 86.7 x 43.2 mm. The guide numbers no bay, so they are em-0 and em-1 from the left. The bays ship with cover panels (QFX5100-EM-BLNK in the datasheet); the modules are ordered separately. The guide says the EX4600 "is configured for the QFX-EM-4Q by default" and also says the modules "are not shipped with the switch", so the shipped state is the cover panel and the 4Q is the module the software expects.

port-lamps.note: Guide Figure 10 and Table 6: two lamps on each SFP+ port, link and activity at the left and status at the right. Figure 11 and Table 7: four lamps on each QSFP+ port, above the upper cage and below the lower one. The photograph shows the same dots; they are 5.8 mm apart on an SFP+ pair and 4.2 mm apart on a QSFP+ row, centred on the printed numeral and on the cage. Lamp positions are estimated; a pixel is 0.3 mm.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal: the SFP+ ports are 0 to 23, even above the cage and odd below it, the numeral between its two lamps, above the upper row and below the lower one; the QSFP+ ports are 24 and 25 in the left column and 26 and 27 in the right, printed at the left of the lamps. Guide figure 9 numbers 0 to 23 and 24 to 27 as well. Interface names are not printed and the guide does not give the xe or et names, so none is written. The guide names the management ports em0 (C0) and em1 (C1), which are written.

ports.note: Front photograph: the SFP+ dot pairs, which are flat on the metal, centre at 22.7, 27.0, 31.2, 35.5, 39.7 and 44.0 mm and again from 114.8 mm on a 14.25 mm pitch, the registry's, to 0.1 mm. The two blocks of six columns have a 6.6 mm gutter. The cage fronts sit 1.2 mm left of the numeral and lamp pair, so the cells start at 14.4 and 106.5 mm. The four QSFP+ cages stand in two columns of two, centred at 209.1 and 238.0 mm, 28.9 mm apart, with the laser warning label to their right. The counts, 24 and 4, are callouts 2 and 3 of figure 9. The QSFP+ pitch is not the registry's 19.0 mm, which is the pitch of a ganged block: these are two columns.

power.note: Guide Table 16 (AC): 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 4.5 A at 100 to 120 VAC and 2.0 A at 200 to 240 VAC, typical 230 W and maximum 365 W. Table 19 (DC): rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating -40 to -72 VDC, 10 A maximum, typical 300 W and maximum 385 W. The datasheet gives a power consumption for one stated load, which is a different scope: 279 W (AFO), 285 W (AFI), 392 W (DC-AFO) and 320 W (DC-AFI) with every fixed port forwarding at line rate with optics, a QSFP+ module and an 8 x 10 GbE module, and two supplies. The tables' typical and maximum are the device's; the datasheet figures are kept as attributes.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 3.298 px/mm, checked against guide Figures 12 to 14: at the left a 63 mm management panel with the four chassis lamps, the SFP management cage C1 with its two lamps, the RJ-45 console jack above the RJ-45 management jack C0 in one shell, the USB port, and the reset pinhole; then five fan slots numbered 0 to 4 on a 49.3 mm pitch, each preceded by a strip carrying its fan symbol, number and lamp; then two supply slots, 0 and 1, the first preceded by its power symbol and number, and at the right edge a strip with the rating legend. The fan modules measure 40.9 x 41.5 mm and the supplies 54.7 mm wide.

rear-photo-vs-drawing.note: Figure 13 prints EX4600-40F on the label plate and the photograph prints EX4600; the photograph is followed, and the plate carries the words RUNNING JUNOS in both. The photograph is of a back-to-front build (AIR IN fan modules, a supply labelled AFI) with one supply and a cover panel in slot 1, and Figure 12 is the same build with two supplies. The default configuration here is the front-to-back AC build; the fan and supply faces are drawn from the AIR IN units and given the AIR OUT legend and orange handles that Tables 11 and 14 state.

row-pitch.note: The two SFP+ cages measure 11.8 and 10.9 mm high with the module bodies in them, tops 13.0 mm apart, so 13.0 mm is the row pitch. The registry's 15.0 mm is measured on another cage and is not a conformance figure. The QSFP+ cages are 14.3 mm apart. Both rows are read off cages with transceivers seated, which hide the openings, so the cell positions are estimated.

sources.note: Juniper EX4600 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2025-08-12, 197 pages (Juniper Networks, copyright 2025): Table 3 (the models), Table 4 (the chassis), the port panel (Figure 9), the port lamps (Figures 10 and 11, Tables 6 and 7), the management panel (Figures 12 to 14, Table 8), the expansion modules (Figures 15 and 16, Tables 9 and 10), the cooling system (Figure 17, Tables 11 to 13) and the power system (Figures 21 to 26, Tables 14 to 19). Juniper EX4600 Ethernet Switch Datasheet, 1000511-016-EN, Sep 2021 (PDF produced 2022-07-25): the specifications, the power consumption by model and the ordering table. Juniper's own studio photographs of the front and the rear, 1500 x 163 and 1500 x 151 px (image library, ex4600-front-high.jpg and ex4600-rear-high.jpg). The held intake folders for the EX and QFX lines were not readable from this work, so no held photograph, stencil or 3D model was used; the public documents above are the only sources. Terms: the documents and photographs are Juniper's, read here for facts only, and nothing of them is copied into the library.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the latch tongues at the foot of every upper SFP+ and QSFP+ cage and at the top of every lower one, so both lips face the band between the rows: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention.

stickers.note: The yellow laser warning label, 5.1 x 26.0 mm at 251.1 across and 6.6 down, and the hazard triangle below it, 7.7 x 7.4 mm at 251.1 and 34.3, are applied labels. They are reserved as regions and not drawn.

vents.note: The photograph shows a honeycomb strip along the top edge, 0.4 to 4.8 mm down, and another along the bottom edge, 40.0 to 43.5 mm, both from 20.3 mm to 246.0 mm, and four hexagonal holes in a column at the left, 8.9 to 13.1 mm across, centred 10.9, 15.9, 21.1 and 26.0 mm down. They are declared vents.
